mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by a housing rebound, resulting in muted S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO monthly declines exceeding 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both CPIAUCSL (below 2%) and FEDFUNDS (below 1%) over three months signals a deflationary easing regime, which historically supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by more than 1% in a month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) and decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous 3-month average AND GDPC1 < previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such savings-driven demand shifts (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1.5% signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5%).
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises by more than 1.5% and CPIAUCSL < 5% (t-test p > 0.05).
